seal/madani/an-nisa|d0|b0.4.1|label: Fighting for Allah; death is by decree and destiny
seal/madani/an-nisa|d0|b0.4.2|text: ﴿وَمَا كَانَ لِمُومِنٍ اَنْ يَّقْتُلَ مُومِناًۖ اِلَّا خَطَـٔاٗۖ﴾
seal/madani/an-nisa|d0|b0.4.3|label: Emigration is the key to provision and a good life
seal/madani/an-nisa|d0|b0.4.4|label: Shortening the prayer, and the prayer of fear
seal/madani/an-nisa|d0|b0.4.4|text: ﴿وَلْتَاتِ طَآئِفَةٌ ا۟خْر۪ىٰ لَمْ يُصَلُّواْ فَلْيُصَلُّواْ مَعَكَ﴾
seal/madani/an-nisa|d0|b0.5|label: The People of the Book and belief in the messengers
seal/madani/an-nisa|d0|b0.5.1|label: Their envy of the blessing of prophethood
seal/madani/an-nisa|d0|b0.5.2|label: Judgement goes by deeds, not by wishful thinking
seal/madani/an-nisa|d0|b0.5.4|label: Sending messengers to establish the proof
seal/madani/an-nisa|d0|b0.5.4|text: ﴿لِيَ۬لَّا يَكُونَ لِلنَّاسِ عَلَى اَ۬للَّهِ حُجَّةُۢ بَعْدَ اَ۬لرُّسُلِۖ﴾
seal/madani/an-nisa|d0|b0.5.5|label: The just word about Isa (peace be upon him)
seal/madani/an-nisa|d0|b0.5.5|text: ﴿إِنَّمَا اَ۬لْمَسِيحُ عِيسَى اَ۪بْنُ مَرْيَمَ رَسُولُ اُ۬للَّهِ﴾
seal/madani/al-maida|lines.0: Type of Surah: Medinan by consensus, revealed after the Hijra and after Surat al-Fath, in separate parts. Its rulings are definitive; nothing in it is abrogated.
seal/madani/al-maida|lines.1: Reason for the name: “al-Ma'idah” (the Table Spread) brings together its axes: the lawful and the unlawful in food, the King (Glorified is He), and fulfilling covenants. Among its names: al-'Uqud (the Contracts), al-Munqidhah (the Rescuer), al-Akhyar (the Righteous).
seal/madani/al-maida|lines.2: Taqwa in the Surah: the measure of fulfilling contracts: not daring to overstep Allah's limits; the lawful is what the King has made lawful, and the unlawful is what He has forbidden.
seal/madani/al-maida|lines.3: The name of Allah that prevails in the Surah: the King (Glorified is He): might, power, wisdom, knowledge and justice.
seal/madani/al-maida|d0|b0|label: Fulfilling contracts with the King ← judgement on the lawful and the unlawful belongs to Him
seal/madani/al-maida|d0|b0.0|text: The circle of the lawful is wide and the circle of the unlawful is narrow. ﴿أُحِلَّتْ لَكُم بَهِيمَةُ اُ۬لَانْعَٰمِ﴾
seal/madani/al-maida|d0|b0.0.0|label: The breadth of the lawful: good things and the food of the People of the Book
seal/madani/al-maida|d0|b0.0.1|text: ﴿فَمَنُ اُ۟ضْطُرَّ فِے مَخْمَصَةٍ غَيْرَ مُتَجَانِفٖ لِّإِثْمٖ﴾
seal/madani/al-maida|d0|b0.0.2|label: Warning against forbidding the lawful out of excess
seal/madani/al-maida|d0|b0.0.2|text: ﴿لَا تُحَرِّمُواْ طَيِّبَٰتِ مَآ أَحَلَّ اَ۬للَّهُ لَكُمْ﴾
seal/madani/al-maida|d0|b0.0.4|label: Hunting: a test of belief in the unseen
seal/madani/al-maida|d0|b0.0.5|label: The bahirah and the sa'ibah: legislation without proof
seal/madani/al-maida|d0|b0.0.5|text: ﴿مَا جَعَلَ اَ۬للَّهُ مِنۢ بَحِيرَةٖ وَلَا سَآئِبَةٖ﴾
seal/madani/al-maida|d0|b0.1|label: Fulfilling contracts and not breaking them
seal/madani/al-maida|d0|b0.1|text: The model of breaking them: the Children of Israel. ﴿وَاذْكُرُواْ نِعْمَةَ اَ۬للَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ وَمِيثَٰقَهُ﴾
seal/madani/al-maida|d0|b0.1.0|label: The covenant: “We hear and we obey”
seal/madani/al-maida|d0|b0.1.0|text: Gratitude for a blessing is the condition for it to last. ﴿إِذْ قُلْتُمْ سَمِعْنَا وَأَطَعْنَاۖ﴾
seal/madani/al-maida|d0|b0.1.1|label: The model of breaking them: the Children of Israel
seal/madani/al-maida|d0|b0.1.1.0|label: Breaking the covenant, forgetting it, and its recompense
seal/madani/al-maida|d0|b0.1.1.0|text: A curse and hardness of hearts, enmity and hatred. ﴿فَبِمَا نَقْضِهِم مِّيثَٰقَهُمْ لَعَنَّٰهُمْ﴾
seal/madani/al-maida|d0|b0.1.1.1|label: The Holy Land: the covenant broken
seal/madani/al-maida|d0|b0.1.1.1|text: Lack of certainty and reliance, so the land was forbidden to them. ﴿فَاذْهَبَ اَنتَ وَرَبُّكَ فَقَٰتِلَآ﴾
seal/madani/al-maida|d0|b0.1.2|label: The sanctity of life and the covenant of peace
seal/madani/al-maida|d0|b0.1.2.0|label: The two sons of Adam: envy before killing
seal/madani/al-maida|d0|b0.1.2.1|label: Armed robbery (hirabah) and theft: the recompense according to the corruption
seal/madani/al-maida|d0|b0.1.3|label: Steadfastness on the covenant of faith
seal/madani/al-maida|d0|b0.1.3|text: Humble towards the believer and mighty against the disbeliever. ﴿فَسَوْفَ يَاتِے اِ۬للَّهُ بِقَوْمٖ يُحِبُّهُمْ وَيُحِبُّونَهُۥٓ﴾
seal/madani/al-maida|d0|b0.2|label: Judging by what Allah has sent down, because He is the King
seal/madani/al-maida|d0|b0.2|text: Departing from it is disbelief, wrongdoing and defiance. ﴿وَمَن لَّمْ يَحْكُم بِمَآ أَنزَلَ اَ۬للَّهُ فَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ اُ۬لْكَٰفِرُونَۖ﴾
seal/madani/al-maida|d0|b0.2.0|label: The King judges between the religious communities
seal/madani/al-maida|d0|b0.2.0|text: What counts is effort and deeds, not affiliation. ﴿وَلِلهِ مُلْكُ اُ۬لسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَالَارْضِ﴾
seal/madani/al-maida|d0|b0.2.1|label: The humanity of Isa (peace be upon him)
seal/madani/al-maida|d0|b0.2.1|text: ﴿لَّقَدْ كَفَرَ اَ۬لذِينَ قَالُوٓاْ إِنَّ اَ۬للَّهَ هُوَ اَ۬لْمَسِيحُ اُ۪بْنُ مَرْيَمَۖ﴾
seal/madani/al-maida|d0|b0.2.2|label: The traits of the hypocrites and the Jews
seal/madani/al-maida|d0|b0.2.2|text: Hastening into disbelief, distortion, and consuming unlawful gain. ﴿لَا يُحْزِنكَ اَ۬لذِينَ يُسَٰرِعُونَ فِے اِ۬لْكُفْرِ﴾
seal/madani/al-maida|d0|b0.2.3|label: The Qur'an confirms and stands guardian over the scriptures
seal/madani/al-maida|d0|b0.2.3|text: ﴿مُصَدِّقاٗ لِّمَا بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ مِنَ اَ۬لْكِتَٰبِ وَمُهَيْمِناً عَلَيْهِۖ﴾
seal/madani/al-maida|d0|b0.2.4|label: Warning against taking the Jews and the Christians as allies
seal/madani/al-maida|d0|b0.2.5|label: The Day of Decision: the truthful benefit from their truthfulness
quiz|1|725e6fe4-21e8-4b10-be63-9d764e773: In the method of reflection (tadabbur) this circle follows, to which verse is the whole Qur'an brought back?
The Verse of the Throne (Ayat al-Kursi)
﴿إِيَّاكَ نَعْبُدُ وَإِيَّاكَ نَسْتَعِينُۖ﴾ (You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help)
The last verse of Surat al-Baqarah
The whole Qur'an goes back to al-Fatiha, so what stays in mind is that all of it is: ﴿إِيَّاكَ نَعْبُدُ وَإِيَّاكَ نَسْتَعِينُۖ﴾ (You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help).
How did al-Fatiha define the straight path that the servant asks for?
As the widest and most beautiful of paths
As a path each person chooses for themselves
As ﴿صِرَٰطَ اَ۬لذِينَ أَنْعَمْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ (the path of those You have blessed)

After ﴿اُ۪هْدِنَا اَ۬لصِّرَٰطَ اَ۬لْمُسْتَقِيمَ﴾ (Guide us to the straight path), He, Glorified be He, defined it by saying: ﴿صِرَٰطَ اَ۬لذِينَ أَنْعَمْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ (the path of those You have blessed).
Where are those who have earned anger and those who are astray in relation to the straight path, as the lesson explained?
On both its sides, to the right and to the left
At its end, once the traveller reaches it
At its start, before the traveller sets out

﴿غَيْرِ اِ۬لْمَغْضُوبِ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا اَ۬لضَّآلِّينَۖ﴾ (not of those who have earned anger, nor of those who are astray): they stand on both sides of the path, lying in wait for whoever walks it; this is the way of trial.
According to the lesson, why is a servant granted success on the path of learning Allah's Book?
Their own effort, might and strength
Being chosen and selected by Allah
Knowledge they already had
The honour of learning Allah's Book comes not from our effort, might or strength, but from Allah choosing and selecting us, so we must remain steadfast on it.
quiz|1|33c19d64-362b-4466-9029-6eadedc6b: Why is the Surah called “the Opening of the Book” (Fatihat al-Kitab)?
Because it is the longest Surah of the Qur'an
Because it is recited at the end of the prayer
Because the Noble Qur'an opens with it
It is so called because the Qur'an opens with it: it opens what follows it in writing, reading, teaching and prayer.
Which of these is not one of the names of Surat al-Fatiha?
The Mother of the Book (Umm al-Kitab)
The Mother of Towns (Umm al-Qura)
The Sufficient (al-Kafiyah)
The Complete (al-Wafiyah)
“The Mother of Towns” is a name of Makkah, which the lesson gave as an example of “mother” meaning what gathers; al-Fatiha is “the Mother of the Book” because it gathers everything in the Qur'an.
What is praise (hamd)?
Extolling the One praised for the perfection of His Essence and His Attributes
A kindness returned for a blessing through action alone
Saying “Praise be to Allah” with the tongue even if the heart does not agree
Praise is extolling and lauding the One praised for the perfection of His Essence and His Attributes; it springs from the heart and is spoken by the tongue.
Which statement about the difference between praise (hamd) and gratitude (shukr) is correct?
Praise is more general than gratitude in its means and more specific in its cause
Praise is more specific than gratitude in its means and more general in its cause
Praise is with the heart and the tongue and is said in ease and in hardship; gratitude is with the heart, the tongue and the limbs and belongs to times of ease.
Which saying is more correct when a calamity strikes?
“O Allah, to You belongs praise”
“O Allah, to You belongs gratitude”
Gratitude belongs to blessings and times of ease, whereas praise is said in ease and in hardship.
In al-Fatiha, seeking Allah's help is built on which attribute?
Divinity (uluhiyyah)
Lordship (rububiyyah)
Mercy
Worship is divinity; seeking help is lordship, because we seek the help of Allah who gives, withholds and benefits by His will; and asking for guidance is mercy.
quiz|1|c0ade183-6fd8-4df8-b8de-32b5c9826: Asking for guidance to the straight path is built on which attribute?
Sovereignty
Lordship
Mercy
﴿إِيَّاكَ نَعْبُدُ﴾ (You alone we worship) is built on divinity, ﴿وَإِيَّاكَ نَسْتَعِينُۖ﴾ (and You alone we ask for help) on lordship, and asking for guidance comes from mercy.
Tawhid of the Names and Attributes belongs to which of the two kinds of tawhid?
Tawhid in knowledge and belief
Tawhid in will and intention
Tawhid in knowledge and belief is the tawhid of the Names and Attributes, concerned with what is reported and known; tawhid in will and intention has two kinds: lordship and divinity.
Praise in al-Fatiha is shown in summary and in detail; what is the summary?
Mentioning the attributes of lordship, mercy and sovereignty
Affirming that praise belongs to Allah in His words ﴿اِ۬لْحَمْدُ لِلهِ﴾ (Praise belongs to Allah)
Asking for guidance to the straight path

The summary is affirming that praise belongs to Allah; He then detailed it by mentioning the attributes that follow: ﴿رَبِّ اِ۬لْعَٰلَمِينَ﴾ ﴿اَ۬لرَّحْمَٰنِ اِ۬لرَّحِيمِ﴾ ﴿مَلِكِ يَوْمِ اِ۬لدِّينِۖ﴾ (Lord of the worlds, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful, King of the Day of Judgement).
Around which attributes do all of Allah's Names and Attributes revolve, as in the lesson?
Two: mercy and sovereignty
Four: divinity, lordship, mercy and sovereignty
Three: knowledge, recognition and lived state
He mentioned praise in summary, then followed it with the attributes; all the Names and Attributes revolve around these four.
Whoever denies the attributes of the One praised is not truly praising, even when saying “Praise be to Allah” with the tongue.
True
False
Praise includes extolling the One praised with His attributes of perfection, so whoever denies His attributes is not praising — including doubting them in times of hardship.
Why did those who have earned anger deserve anger, as the lesson explained?
Because knowledge never reached them
Because they lost the way out of ignorance
Because they knew and did not act

﴿غَيْرِ اِ۬لْمَغْضُوبِ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ (not of those who have earned anger): they knew, recognised and affirmed tawhid in the Names and Attributes and in lordship, but did not act, so they deserved anger.
quiz|1|c2ffa56b-bc81-40a8-857c-d9a7c15c3: Why can no one but Allah fully count His praise?
Because the tongue is enough for praise
Because of the perfection and the great number of His attributes
Because praise belongs only to times of ease

The more the attributes of perfection of the One praised, the more complete His praise; and we cannot count His attributes nor His blessings: ﴿وَإِن تَعُدُّواْ نِعْمَةَ اَ۬للَّهِ لَا تُحْصُوهَآۖ﴾ (and if you count the blessings of Allah, you could not number them).
Which of these is not truly praising?
Someone who praises Allah in hardship as in ease
Someone who admits being unable to count Allah's blessings
Someone who turns away from loving Allah and submitting to Him
Whoever denies the attributes of the One praised is not praising, nor is whoever turns away from loving Him and submitting to Him.
How did Allah condemn the gods of the disbelievers?
By stripping them of every attribute of perfection: they neither hear, see, guide, benefit nor harm
By their small number
By their being recently made
What neither hears, sees, benefits nor harms does not deserve to be a god, so humility is shown to Allah alone.
How does Allah love His servant to come before Him, as the lesson quoted from Ibn al-Qayyim?
As a king comes before a king, confident in their many deeds
As someone who thinks their deeds have earned them Paradise
As a servant comes before the King, humble and broken
“Allah loves you to come before Him as a servant comes before the King, and does not love you to come before Him as a king comes before a king”; humility and submission are the reality of servitude.
A servant can praise Allah as He truly deserves by worshipping a great deal.
True
False
We cannot fully count His praise because we do not encompass His Names nor His blessings; the servant's sense of falling short in praise is what fulfils servitude.
quiz|1|438eb264-b983-4146-b0f5-c96524309: What does “the Lord” (al-Rabb) mean?
The One who nurtures others and brings them up step by step
The One who gives at once everything asked of Him
The One who alone owns the Day of Judgement
The Lord is the One who nurtures His servants and brings them up step by step; the heart of nurturing is wisdom in withholding and giving.
What is specific lordship?
Allah creating and providing for all creatures
Guiding every creature to what is good for it in this world
His nurturing His believing allies with faith, and removing the distractions and obstacles that stand between them and Him

General lordship is creation, provision and guidance to worldly good for all; specific lordship is the nurturing of His allies: He nurtures them with faith, perfects them and removes distractions and obstacles from them.
Iblis's prayer ﴿رَبِّ فَأَنظِرْنِےٓ إِلَىٰ يَوْمِ يُبْعَثُونَۖ﴾ (My Lord, then grant me respite until the Day they are raised): from which of the two lordships was its answer?
General lordship
Specific lordship
Its answer was a worldly gift, a gift of abandonment that shows no love, so it comes from general lordship.
Why is the lordship in ﴿رَبِّ اِ۬لْعَٰلَمِينَ﴾ (Lord of the worlds) a general lordship?
Because it is specific to the prophets and the allies of Allah
Because “the worlds” are everything other than Allah: believer and disbeliever, humans, jinn and inanimate things
Because it concerns the Hereafter alone
He, Glorified be He, is the Lord of everything other than Allah; He gives and withholds in measure, by His knowledge and wisdom, and it allows no comparison in love or rank.
Receiving much of this world is a sign that Allah loves a person.
True
False
Worldly gifts come from general lordship, which includes the righteous and the wicked, the believer and the disbeliever, so they show neither love nor dislike.
quiz|1|96f02b47-426d-4868-9e86-e3efbf120: For whom is general lordship?
For the believers and the allies of Allah alone
For all creation, believers and disbelievers alike
For the prophets alone
General lordship is for all people, righteous and wicked; through it He creates them, provides for them and guides them to what is good for their worldly life.
What does specific lordship concern?
The good of religion and the Hereafter: Allah nurtures His allies with faith and grants them success in it
Worldly good such as wealth, food and drink
The movement of the sun and the moon in their orbits
Specific lordship is Allah's nurturing of His believing allies with what sets right their religion and their Hereafter; general lordship is for worldly good.
Allah gave Iblis what he asked for when he said: ﴿رَبِّ فَأَنظِرْنِےٓ إِلَىٰ يَوْمِ يُبْعَثُونَۖ﴾ (My Lord, then grant me respite until the Day they are raised). What does this gift show?
Allah's love for him and pleasure with him
That it was a gift of general lordship that shows no love; rather, it was a gift of abandonment
That he is one of Allah's allies
Worldly gifts through general lordship show no love, and the gift to Iblis was a gift of abandonment.
“The more of this world a servant is given, the more it shows that Allah loves them.”
True
False

General lordship concerns worldly matters, so it shows neither love nor dislike; what counts is what the servant does with the gift: does it help them toward their Hereafter or stand between them and it?

Why is the prayer ﴿وَمِنْهُم مَّنْ يَّقُولُ رَبَّنَآ ءَاتِنَا فِے اِ۬لدُّنْي۪ا حَسَنَةٗ وَفِے اِ۬لَاخِرَةِ حَسَنَةٗ وَقِنَا عَذَابَ اَ۬لنّ۪ارِۖ﴾ (And among them are those who say: Our Lord, give us good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and protect us from the punishment of the Fire) a prayer by specific lordship?
Because the one praying named what they want from this world and made it a condition
Because “good” comes indefinite and without condition, so the one praying leaves to Allah what He knows to be good, even if it does not look so to them
Because it asks for this world alone

The one praying did not specify the good nor set conditions on it, but entrusted the matter to the Nurturer, Glorified be He, as with the cave, which outwardly looked like harm but was in truth mercy.
Which of these is not one of the names that fall under His name “the Lord” (al-Rabb)?
The Provider (al-Razzaq)
The Originator (al-Bari')
The Especially Merciful (al-Rahim)
The Expander (al-Basit)
Under the name “the Lord” are His actions toward His servants: He creates, originates, provides, gives, withholds, constricts and expands; the Especially Merciful is one of the names of mercy.
quiz|1|19bd90d0-2283-4a1a-9489-358cd51bd: Which of Allah's two names points to the general mercy for all creation?
The Especially Merciful (al-Rahim)
The Most Merciful (al-Rahman)
Mercy has two kinds: general, for all creation, by His name the Most Merciful (al-Rahman); and specific, for the believers, by His name the Especially Merciful (al-Rahim).
Which of these is not a trait of general mercy?
Through it Allah answers the prayer of a disbeliever in distress
Through it a disbeliever lives safe, sound and healthy
It is a sign of Allah's love and pleasure
It covers humans and animals
General mercy concerns worldly matters only, so it is not a sign of Allah's love and pleasure.

Allah says: ﴿وَإِذَا مَسَّكُمُ اُ۬لضُّرُّ فِے اِ۬لْبَحْرِ ضَلَّ مَن تَدْعُونَ إِلَّآ إِيَّاهُۖ﴾ (And when harm touches you at sea, those you call upon vanish, except Him). By which mercy does Allah answer the prayer of these disbelievers in their distress?
By general mercy
By specific mercy
By general mercy Allah answers the prayer of a disbeliever in distress and saves them; then many of them go back to what they were doing.
“The specific mercy for the believers is a sign of Allah's love and pleasure.”
True
False
Specific mercy is for His believing servants, His allies and His prophets; by it He guides them to what benefits them in their Hereafter, so it is a sign of love.
Why should we not compare people by what they have been given of this world?
Because only the believer is given this world
Because Allah gives the disbeliever nothing
Because worldly gifts come from general mercy, so they are no sign of Allah's love or pleasure
General mercy covers even animals; just as we do not compare ourselves with beasts, we do not compare people by worldly gifts whose wisdom we do not know.
quiz|1|86bc792a-baec-4ad7-93e1-bca36ea9b: “Specific mercy may come in a form the servant does not like or ask for, like the well, the prison and the cave.”
True
False
Specific mercy may not look like mercy on the outside; it is where faith in divine decree shows: being certain that it is mercy.
Why does the name “al-Rahman” (the Most Merciful) come on the pattern “fa'lan”?
Because it is specific to the believers alone
To show that mercy is little
To show vastness and fullness of the attribute of mercy
The pattern fa'lan expresses vastness and fullness, as “ghadban” is said of someone full of anger; Allah, Glorified be He, is full of the attribute of mercy.
Allah says: ﴿اَ۬لرَّحْمَٰنُ عَلَى اَ۬لْعَرْشِ اِ۪سْتَو۪ىٰۖ﴾ (The Most Merciful rose over the Throne). Why is rising over the Throne joined to the name “the Most Merciful”?
Because the Most Merciful is a name specific to the Hereafter
Because the Throne encompasses all creatures and mercy is vast for them, so He rose over the vastest of creatures with the vastest of attributes
Because the Throne is specific to the believers
The Throne encompasses creation and contains it, and mercy encompasses creation, as Allah says: “My mercy encompasses all things.”
Which of these is one of the names that fall under His names “the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful”?
The Nourisher (al-Muqit)
The Loving (al-Wadud)
The Reckoner (al-Hasib)

The Loving shows love to His servants and draws them near; it is one of the names of mercy along with the Subtle, the Forbearing, the All-Forgiving and the Appreciative, whereas the Nourisher and the Reckoner fall under the name “the King”.
The well into which Yusuf (peace be upon him) was thrown: which mercy was it?
General mercy
Specific mercy
The end of the story shows it was specific mercy, since Yusuf finally became a prophet and a king, even if it did not look like mercy on the outside.
The treasures of Qarun, longed for by those who wanted the life of this world: which mercy were they?
Specific mercy
General mercy
The earth swallowing him showed it was general mercy; the end in this world points to what will happen in the Hereafter.
quiz|1|df40fb0c-f76e-4e51-961b-a109b868c: What is the difference between “the King” (al-Malik) and “the Owner” (al-Malik)?
The King owns, and the Owner rules
There is no difference
The King rules, and the Owner owns
“King” comes from ruling and “Owner” from owning; a person may rule what they do not own and own what they do not rule, but Allah both owns and rules.
Allah says: ﴿لَّهُۥ مَا فِے اِ۬لسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِے اِ۬لَارْضِۖ﴾ (To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth). Which of the two names shows in this verse?
The King
The Owner
The “la” in “lahu” (to Him) expresses ownership: He, Glorified be He, owns what is in the heavens and what is on the earth.
Allah says: ﴿اِنِ اِ۬لْحُكْمُ إِلَّا لِلهِۖ﴾ (Judgement belongs to Allah alone). Which of the two names shows in this verse?
The Owner
The King
Judgement belongs to Allah alone; He is the King who governs the kingdom of the heavens and the earth.
The verses of recompense, of deciding and judging between servants, point to His name:
The Most Merciful (al-Rahman)
The King (al-Malik)
The Originator (al-Bari')
Allah judges between servants and recompenses the people of misguidance and the people of faith; this matter of recompense falls under His name the King.
Which of these is one of the names that fall under His name “the King”?
The Gatherer (al-Jami')
The Kind (al-Ra'uf)
The Loving (al-Wadud)
The Gatherer is one of the names of sovereignty: “the Gatherer of people for a Day about which there is no doubt”; the Kind and the Loving are names of mercy.
“Allah's mercy outstrips His anger: mercy is His constant attribute, and anger is for whoever has earned it.”
True
False
In every situation Allah's mercy comes before His anger; if a servant earns anger, the blame is theirs, like Pharaoh, to whom Allah sent a prophet so that he might believe.
quiz|1|7a90faed-99ba-4222-9e4f-df134d89d: In His words ﴿إِيَّاكَ نَعْبُدُ وَإِيَّاكَ نَسْتَعِينُۖ﴾ (You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help), which part rises from the servant to their Lord?
“You alone we worship”
“And You alone we ask for help”
Servitude rises from the servant as humility and obedience, and success and help come down to them from Allah.
What does placing “You alone” (iyyaka) before the verb in “You alone we worship” convey?
That we worship Allah and others along with Him
Exclusivity and restriction: we worship none but You and seek help from none but You
Putting the servant's action before Allah's name
Saying “we worship Allah” does not rule out worshipping others, whereas “You alone we worship” restricts it: we worship You alone.
Which of these is not one of the secrets of placing “iyyaka” first?
Ruling out every object of worship besides Him
Courtesy toward Allah by putting His name before our action
Exclusivity, called restriction
Putting the servant's action first because it matters more than the One worshipped

His name, Glorified be He, is placed before our action out of courtesy toward Him; it carries restriction and rules out every object of worship besides Him — it does not put the servant's action first.
What does worship mean in “You alone we worship”?
Asking for help and success
Knowing the Names without acting
Obedience, humility before Allah and surrender to His command
Worship is obedience and humility: Allah's command finds you surrendered to it like a feather in the wind; asking for help is seeking help (isti'anah).
Is servitude complete with love alone, without fear?
Yes, love is enough
No, fear is one of the pillars of servitude along with love, and its finest form is the fear of reverence and awe
Worshipping Allah with love alone is not of the Sunnah; fear includes the fear of reverence and awe as well as fear of His punishment and of a bad end.
quiz|1|9552e97c-3201-4850-a9de-1d316fc83: What does seeking help (isti'anah) mean, as explained in the lesson?
Extolling Allah with His attributes of perfection
Asking for help in order to be able to do something and to manage doing it
Abandoning the means while waiting for relief
Seeking help is asking Allah for help so that we are able to do something and manage it, because we can do nothing without His help and the success He grants.
Seeking Allah's help is part of worship.
True
False
Asking Allah for help with humility before Him is worship, which is why “You alone we ask for help” falls within “You alone we worship”.
“You alone we worship” is the cure for which disease of the heart?
Arrogance and self-admiration
Ignorance and misguidance
Showing off (riya')
“Iyyaka” means You alone: whoever is sincere in it devotes worship purely to Allah and is freed from showing off, which is the lesser shirk.
Why is “You alone we ask for help” the cure for arrogance and self-admiration?
Because the servant attributes every success to Allah and disowns any might or strength of their own
Because it is said seventeen times a day in the prayer
Because through it the servant no longer needs to take the means
Because it comes after “You alone we worship”
Whoever says “You alone we ask for help” sincerely knows that all they achieved is by Allah's grace and help, and so does not say: I did it.

In the prayer of Yusuf (peace be upon him), ﴿رَبِّ قَدَ اٰتَيْتَنِے مِنَ اَ۬لْمُلْكِ وَعَلَّمْتَنِے مِن تَاوِيلِ اِ۬لَاحَادِيثِۖ فَاطِرَ اَ۬لسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَالَارْضِ أَنتَ وَلِيِّۦ فِے اِ۬لدُّنْي۪ا وَالَاخِرَةِ تَوَفَّنِے مُسْلِماٗ وَأَلْحِقْنِے بِالصَّٰلِحِينَۖ﴾ (My Lord, You have given me of sovereignty and taught me of the interpretation of events. Originator of the heavens and the earth, You are my protector in this world and the Hereafter. Take my soul as a Muslim and join me with the righteous), to whom did he attribute the sovereignty and knowledge he received?
To his own effort and knowledge
To Allah alone
To the people of Egypt who put him in charge
He attained sovereignty and learned the interpretation of events, yet he attributed everything to Allah and did not say: I got there; this is the reality of “You alone we ask for help”.
If Allah gives a person wealth and status in this world, what does that show?
That Allah loves them
That they are a believer
It shows no love, for Allah gives this world to the believer and the disbeliever

The means of this world are made available to the believer and the disbeliever through Allah's lordship and general mercy; Allah gives this world to those He loves and those He does not, so a gift is no sign of love.
quiz|1|f1567742-7b60-4c55-aadc-51e51cea5: Which of these verses joins worship and reliance, just as al-Fatiha joins “You alone we worship” and “You alone we ask for help”?
﴿فَضَرَبْنَا عَلَىٰٓ ءَاذَانِهِمْ فِے اِ۬لْكَهْفِ سِنِينَ عَدَداٗ﴾ (So We sealed their ears in the cave for a number of years)

﴿وَلِلهِ غَيْبُ اُ۬لسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَالَارْضِۖ وَإِلَيْهِ يُرْجَعُ اُ۬لَامْرُ كُلُّهُۥۖ فَاعْبُدْهُ وَتَوَكَّلْ عَلَيْهِۖ﴾ (To Allah belongs the unseen of the heavens and the earth, and to Him the whole matter returns; so worship Him and rely on Him)
﴿يَٰنَارُ كُونِے بَرْداٗ وَسَلَٰماً عَلَىٰٓ إِبْرَٰهِيمَۖ﴾ (O fire, be coolness and safety for Ibrahim)
“So worship Him” is a command to fulfil “You alone we worship”, and “and rely on Him” is a command to fulfil “You alone we ask for help”.
In “so worship Him and rely on Him”, “and rely on Him” is a command to fulfil which of the two?
“You alone we worship”
“You alone we ask for help”
Reliance (tawakkul) is depending on Allah and entrusting the matter to Him, and by it “You alone we ask for help” is fulfilled.

What is the difference between the words of Shu'ayb (peace be upon him) ﴿وَمَا تَوْفِيقِيَ إِلَّا بِاللَّهِۖ عَلَيْهِ تَوَكَّلْتُۖ وَإِلَيْهِ أُنِيبُۖ﴾ (My success is only through Allah; in Him I trust and to Him I turn) and Allah's words ﴿رَّبُّ اُ۬لْمَشْرِقِ وَالْمَغْرِبِۖ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَۖ فَاتَّخِذْهُ وَكِيلاٗۖ﴾ (Lord of the east and the west; there is no god but He, so take Him as your Trustee)?
The first is about worship and the second about seeking help
There is no difference
In Shu'ayb's words he himself fulfilled “You alone we ask for help”; the second is Allah's command to the servant to fulfil it
Shu'ayb's words report a prophet who fulfilled seeking help, whereas “so take Him as your Trustee” is Allah's command to the servant to fulfil “You alone we ask for help”.
By which words in al-Fatiha is the tawhid of divinity fulfilled?
“You alone we worship”
“King of the Day of Judgement”
“Guide us to the straight path”
The tawhid of divinity: none is truly worshipped but Allah; we fulfil it in al-Fatiha by saying “You alone we worship”.
What does it mean for a servant to take Allah as Trustee (wakil)?
To stop working and settle for supplication
To ask Allah for specific things in every detail
To entrust their affairs to Allah, trusting Him and relying on Him
A trustee is entrusted with the matter because they defend you better than you defend yourself; once trust and reliance are there, “You alone we ask for help” is there.
quiz|1|06e547ee-870d-456e-85fa-bb332ff8d: Which of these is not one of the pillars of servitude?
Love
Hope
Reliance
Fear
The pillars of servitude are fear, hope and love; reliance is one of the pillars of seeking help.
What is the spirit of worship and the head of all forms of servitude?
Fear of punishment
Love
Longing for reward
The greatest servitude is to worship Allah out of love and reverence, even if there were no punishment and no reward; the spirit of worship is love.
What are the two pillars of seeking help?
Sincerity and following
Fear and hope
Trust and reliance
Seeking help is trust and reliance: we trust Allah, so we rely on Him; true reliance comes after trust.
Servitude goes from the servant to Allah, and help goes from Allah to the servant.
True
False
The servant turns to Allah with worship, and help and success come down from Allah to the servant.
Where does trust in Allah come from?
From knowing His Most Beautiful Names and Attributes as they show in the stories of the Qur'an and in people's experiences
From the many means a person holds
From being given everything one asks for
When we come to know Allah through experiences and the stories of the Qur'an as Lord, Most Merciful, Especially Merciful and King, we become certain of His Names and so we trust Him.
quiz|1|6e1c9d86-19c5-4b52-bf6f-d42a09248: What are the two foundations of servitude?
Trust and reliance
Sincerity and following
Fear and hope
The foundations of servitude are sincerity and following: worship is fulfilled only when it is for Allah alone and done as He commanded.
What does placing “You alone” (iyyaka) before “we worship” convey?
Exclusivity: we worship no one but You
Stressing the great amount of worship
That worship comes after seeking help
Placing it first is a means of exclusivity: “iyyaka” means You alone, and this is sincerity: I worship none but You and I do not show off.
Which of these is not one of the kinds of people according to sincerity and following?
Sincerity without following
Following without sincerity
Neither sincerity nor following
Knowledge without action
According to sincerity and following, people are of four kinds: sincerity with following, neither sincerity nor following, sincerity without following, and following without sincerity.
The people of sincerity and following act to win people's thanks and praise.
True
False
All their deeds are for Allah; they want neither reward nor thanks from people, nor standing with them, nor praise.

Why did Musa (peace be upon him), after watering the flock for the two young women, say: ﴿ثُمَّ تَوَلّ۪ىٰٓ إِلَى اَ۬لظِّلِّ فَقَالَ رَبِّ إِنِّے لِمَآ أَنزَلْتَ إِلَيَّ مِنْ خَيْرٖ فَقِيرٞۖ﴾ (Then he withdrew to the shade and said: My Lord, I am truly in need of whatever good You send down to me)?
To ask them for a wage for the watering
Because he did not know the way to Madyan
So that arrogance would not creep in after he had given and helped
In the moment of giving, the self feels strong and grows arrogant, so he sought Allah's help and showed his need of Him; “You alone we ask for help” is the cure for arrogance.
quiz|1|9ac43f73-e3a6-4e26-9791-b5af93b74: Why should people's injustice and wrongdoing not stop you from spending on them?
Because spending is for Allah, not for them
Because they will thank you in the end
Because spending protects you from their harm
A deed done for Allah expects no reward or thanks from people, so their injustice does not cut it off.
What question should be asked of oneself when angry?
Do people know what was done to me?
Does what angered me anger Allah?
If what angered you angers Allah, be angry for Allah's sake; if it does not anger Him and only angers you for your own sake, stop and restrain yourself.
A friend visiting others and not you
Someone not returning a favour you did for them
Sins such as abandoning the prayer or deliberately breaking the fast in Ramadan are what anger Allah; the rest are worldly matters we get angry about for our own sake.
Being angry because so-and-so did not give me anything is anger for Allah's sake.
This is anger over a worldly matter concerning oneself, not something that angers Allah, so the self should be restrained at such a time.
quiz|1|28ba6428-52f9-4315-bfbf-ad20c50d5: Who are the people of “sincerity without following”, as the lesson describes them?
Show-offs who perfect the outward form of worship so that they are called devout
Ignorant devotees who worship Allah in ways He did not prescribe, thinking it brings them closer to Him
Those who neither worship Allah nor seek His help

They are the ignorant devotees, like someone who thinks continuous fasting without breaking it, or fasting on the day of Eid, brings them closer to Allah: their intention is for Allah, but their deed lacks following.

The lesson cites His words ﴿وَمَآ أُمِرُوٓاْ إِلَّا لِيَعْبُدُواْ اُ۬للَّهَ مُخْلِصِينَ لَهُ اُ۬لدِّينَ﴾ (And they were commanded only to worship Allah, devoting the religion sincerely to Him) to reject the deeds of which group?
Sincerity without following
Neither sincerity nor following
Following without sincerity

The deeds of the people of following without sincerity outwardly agree with the Shari'ah, but they are for other than Allah, so they are not accepted, because Allah commanded that religion be devoted sincerely to Him.

Who have the fullest share of His words ﴿اَ۬لذِينَ يَفْرَحُونَ بِمَآ أَتَواْ وَّيُحِبُّونَ أَنْ يُّحْمَدُواْ بِمَا لَمْ يَفْعَلُواْ فَلَا تَحْسِبَنَّهُم بِمَفَازَةٖ مِّنَ اَ۬لْعَذَابِۖ وَلَهُمْ عَذَابٌ اَلِيمٞۖ﴾ (Those who rejoice in what they have done and love to be praised for what they have not done — do not think them safe from the punishment; theirs is a painful punishment)?
The people of “neither sincerity nor following”, among innovators who show off
The people of sincerity and following
Ignorant devotees who erred out of ignorance
Their deeds neither agree with the Shari'ah nor are purely for Allah, and they love to be praised for following and sincerity that they have not practised.
Among the best things to ask Allah for is help in what pleases Him, as in “O Allah, help me to remember You, to thank You and to worship You well.”
True
False
The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) taught it to Mu'adh to say after every prayer; it is seeking help for worship, so it is among the most beneficial supplications.
Allah gave Iblis what he asked for. What is understood from this?
That Allah loves everyone whose prayer He answers
That worldly gifts come from general lordship, given to the righteous and the wicked, and show no love
That Iblis asked for what would help him toward pleasing Allah
The creature most hated by Allah asked Him and He gave to him, so worldly gifts show neither love nor dislike; indeed it only took him further away, because it was no help toward what pleases Allah.
Which of these is not a trait of the people of “You alone we worship” without “You alone we ask for help” (the Qadariyyah)?
They hold that the servant does everything by their own might and strength
They say Allah treated His allies and His enemies alike in help
They believe Allah grants extra success to whom He wills
The Qadariyyah deny specific success and the withdrawal of support, so they are left to themselves, and the way of seeking help is closed to them.
quiz|1|00e54333-0373-4c99-a127-2979bc921: What is general guidance?
Allah guiding every creature to what it was created for
Guiding the believers alone to the path of Paradise
The messengers making truth clear from falsehood
Everything in the heavens and the earth Allah created for something and guided it to fulfil it; this is general guidance.
What is the order of the levels of specific guidance, as the lesson explained?
Success granted, then clarification, then steadfastness
Clarification, then success granted, then steadfastness
Steadfastness, then clarification, then success granted
First the path is made clear by its signs, then the traveller needs success granted, then steadfastness until arriving.
What do His words ﴿وَمَا كُنَّا مُعَذِّبِينَ حَتَّىٰ نَبْعَثَ رَسُولاٗۖ﴾ (And We never punish until We have sent a messenger) show?
That the guidance of clarification alone is enough to enter Paradise
That Allah punishes no one before clarification has reached them
That granting success is in the hands of the messengers
The guidance of clarification is Allah's proof against creation, so He punishes no one until it has reached them; this is part of His justice.
In His words ﴿وَإِنَّكَ لَتَهْدِےٓ إِلَىٰ صِرَٰطٖ مُّسْتَقِيمٖ﴾ (And you truly guide to a straight path), which guidance is attributed to the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him)?
The guidance of clarification and direction
The guidance of success granted
General guidance
The guidance attributed to the Messenger is clarification: he points to the path and makes it clear, and “your duty is only to convey”.

In His words ﴿إِنَّكَ لَا تَهْدِے مَنَ اَحْبَبْتَۖ وَلَٰكِنَّ اَ۬للَّهَ يَهْدِے مَنْ يَّشَآءُۖ وَهُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِالْمُهْتَدِينَۖ﴾ (You cannot guide whom you love, but Allah guides whom He wills, and He knows best those who are guided), which guidance is denied to the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him)?
The guidance of clarification
General guidance
The guidance of success granted
Granting success is in Allah's hands alone; had it been in the Messenger's hands he would have guided his uncle; as for clarification, he conveyed it.
The guidance of success granted is more general than the guidance of clarification, so it is for all people.
True
False

Clarification is for all people, whereas success granted is more specific; it comes to whoever takes up the clarification: ﴿وَيَزِيدُ اُ۬للَّهُ اُ۬لذِينَ اَ۪هْتَدَوْاْ هُدىٗۖ﴾ (And Allah increases in guidance those who are guided).
quiz|1|ad655080-1941-46aa-9d43-ff5384a73: In His words ﴿وَمَا كَانَ اَ۬للَّهُ لِيُضِلَّ قَوْماَۢ بَعْدَ إِذْ هَد۪يٰهُمْ حَتَّىٰ يُبَيِّنَ لَهُم مَّا يَتَّقُونَۖ﴾ (Allah would not lead a people astray after He has guided them until He makes clear to them what they should guard against), what does Allah leading them astray mean?
A punishment for them, after He made things clear and they did not act on it
Leading astray from the outset, before any clarification reached them
That they never knew the path at all
Allah never led a people astray except after making clear to them what to guard against; when they did not accept it, He punished them by leading them astray.
In His words ﴿فَلَمَّا زَاغُوٓاْ أَزَاغَ اَ۬للَّهُ قُلُوبَهُمْۖ﴾ (So when they swerved, Allah made their hearts swerve), what came first?
Allah making their hearts swerve
Their own swerving from the clarification after they had seen it
Punishment coming down on them
They saw the clarification and swerved from it, so Allah making their hearts swerve was a recompense for their swerving.

Allah says ﴿وَأَمَّا ثَمُودُ فَهَدَيْنَٰهُمْ فَاسْتَحَبُّواْ اُ۬لْعَم۪ىٰ عَلَى اَ۬لْهُد۪ىٰ﴾ (As for Thamud, We guided them, but they preferred blindness over guidance). What guidance did Thamud receive?
The guidance of clarification: they knew the path and did not follow it
The guidance of success granted, until they arrived
General guidance alone
Clarification reached them from their prophet and through the she-camel, but they preferred blindness over guidance.
What does it mean that the guidance of clarification is “a condition, not a cause”?
That whoever sees the clarification is certain to be guided
That it is not needed by whoever wants guidance
That it is indispensable but not enough until the servant takes it up, and then success is granted
Not everyone who sees the sign arrives; if following does not go with the clarification, success granted and complete guidance are not obtained.
Allah sealed their hearts from the outset, before they disbelieved.
True
False
Allah says ﴿بَلْ طَبَعَ اَ۬للَّهُ عَلَيْهَا بِكُفْرِهِمْ﴾ (Rather, Allah has sealed them because of their disbelief), so the sealing is a recompense for their disbelief and their persisting in it.
What kind of guidance is in His words ﴿اَ۬لذِے خَلَقَ فَسَوّ۪ىٰ﴾ ﴿وَالذِے قَدَّرَ فَهَد۪ىٰ﴾ (who created and proportioned, and who determined and guided)?
General guidance for all creatures
The guidance of clarification
The guidance of steadfastness
Allah created everything, proportioned it, determined it and guided it to what sets it right, like the earth in its turning and the heart in its beating; this is general guidance.
quiz|1|52279549-cff5-4f9f-8348-c6497008d: What is “the path” (al-sirat)?
Any way people take
The clear way with no crookedness in it
The way most people take
The Arabs call a way “sirat” only when it is clear and straight, not crooked, unlike “sabil”, which may be crooked.
Which of these is not one of the five things the path (al-sirat) includes?
Straightness
Leading to the goal
Many travellers on it
Nearness
The five are: straightness, leading to the goal, nearness, room for those who pass, and being clearly defined; the people of the path are few in every age.
Why is the straight path the shortest way to the goal?
Because a straight line is the shortest line between two points, and the more crooked a way is, the longer it gets
Because it is the widest way
Because it is the easiest way with the fewest obstacles
The more crooked a way is, the longer and farther it gets; this is why the Qur'an describes misguidance as far.
What is the first benefit of linking the path to those who have been blessed in ﴿صِرَٰطَ اَ۬لذِينَ أَنْعَمْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ (the path of those You have blessed)?
Removing the loneliness of being alone and urging to catch up with them
Showing that the people of truth are the most numerous
Naming those who walk it in our time
People are by nature lonely when alone, so Allah reminds of the company of the prophets, the truthful, the martyrs and the righteous.
In the parable of a man going out to the prayer who is confronted by a human devil, what lets him reach his destination?
Stopping and answering back until he wins
Turning away from him and keeping to what he set out to do
Going back home
Turning toward the enemy delays him and makes the enemy covet him; but if he turns away and keeps to what he set out to do, the enemy cannot get from him what it wants.
The gazelle is faster than the dog, so why does the dog catch it?
Because the dog is stronger
Because it turns to look at the dog and its running weakens
Because it stops to rest
When the gazelle senses the dog, it turns to look at it, its running weakens and the dog catches it; in the same way, turning aside delays the traveller from the goal.
quiz|1|7e7d3189-a93e-4113-8def-f54e54d05: What is the seeking of nearness (tawassul) in His words ﴿صِرَٰطَ اَ۬لذِينَ أَنْعَمْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ (the path of those You have blessed)?
Approaching Allah through His blessing on those He guided: bless us as You blessed them
Approaching Him through the great number of our good deeds
Approaching Him through living persons
It is like a beggar saying “Give to me among those to whom You have given”: it is approaching Allah through His blessings and His kindness.
What precedes the request for guidance in al-Fatiha?
Mentioning worldly needs first
Nothing, because it is the greatest of requests
Praise and extolling of Allah, then mention of servitude and tawhid
Allah taught His servants to approach Him through His Names and Attributes and through their servitude before saying: Guide us to the straight path.
Who are “those who have earned anger”, according to the division of people by knowledge and action?
Those who act without knowledge
Those who know the truth and go against it
Those who know and act
Whoever knows the truth and goes against it deserves anger, having known the path and not taken it.
Who are “those who are astray” in His words ﴿وَلَا اَ۬لضَّآلِّينَۖ﴾ (nor of those who are astray)?
The people of knowledge and action
Those who know and do not act
The ignorant who act without knowledge
Those who are astray do act, but their problem is that they lack knowledge, so they need someone to teach them.
Why is the doer of blessing named in “You have blessed”, while the doer of anger is left out in “those who have earned anger”?
Because anger never comes from Allah at all
Because blessing is goodness and grace while anger is justice, and leaving out the doer of anger humbles those who have earned it
Only because the wording is shorter

Allah attributed to Himself the more perfect of the two; naming the doer of blessing honours those who have been blessed, and leaving out the doer of anger signals the disgrace of those who have earned it.
Allah alone is the source of blessings, whereas in anger His angels and His allies share, being angry when He is angry.
True
False
Allah says ﴿وَمَا بِكُم مِّن نِّعْمَةٖ فَمِنَ اَ۬للَّهِۖ﴾ (Whatever blessing you have is from Allah), so He alone is the source of blessing, whereas anger is not His alone.
quiz|1|final|0|q: On which three attributes is Surat al-Fatiha built?
quiz|1|final|0|why: “You alone we worship” is built on divinity, “You alone we ask for help” on lordship, and the request for guidance on mercy.
quiz|1|final|1|q: What do general lordship, general mercy and general guidance have in common?
quiz|1|final|1|c0: They are specific to the believers and show Allah's love
quiz|1|final|1|c1: They are for all creatures in worldly matters, and show neither love nor dislike
quiz|1|final|1|c2: They exist only in the Hereafter
quiz|1|final|1|why: Through them the righteous and the wicked are given, the disbeliever is provided for and creatures are guided to what is good for them, so they cannot be taken as proof of Allah's pleasure.
quiz|1|final|2|q: Which of these is not part of the “specific” that Allah reserves for His allies and that shows His love?
quiz|1|final|2|why: General guidance is for all beings, whereas specific lordship, specific mercy and the guidance of success granted are for the believers.
quiz|1|final|3|q: Why does “You alone we worship” come before “You alone we ask for help”?
quiz|1|final|3|c0: Because worship is the goal and seeking help is the means to it: we seek help in order to worship
quiz|1|final|3|c1: Because seeking help is not part of worship
quiz|1|final|3|c2: Because worship is easier than seeking help
quiz|1|final|3|why: One of the secrets of the order is putting goals before means: worship is the goal of the servants, and seeking help is the means to it.
quiz|1|final|4|q: What is the difference between the pillars of servitude and its foundations?
quiz|1|final|4|c0: Its pillars are trust and reliance; its foundations are love and fear
quiz|1|final|4|c1: Its pillars are love, fear and hope; its foundations are sincerity and following
quiz|1|final|4|c2: Its pillars are sincerity and following; its foundations are love and hope
quiz|1|final|4|why: Servitude stands on love, fear and hope, and is accepted only with sincerity and following; trust and reliance are the two pillars of seeking help.
quiz|1|final|5|q: How did the lessons bring together Allah's will and the servant's choice in guidance?
quiz|1|final|5|c0: Allah forces some people to believe and others to disbelieve
quiz|1|final|5|c1: The servant is guided by themselves, and Allah's will plays no part
quiz|1|final|5|c2: Allah made the path clear to all, grants success to whoever takes up the clarification, and abandons whoever turns away, so that leading them astray is a punishment
quiz|1|final|5|why: The guidance of clarification is a proof against all people, success is for whoever follows it, leading astray comes only after clarification, and Allah forces no one.
quiz|1|final|6|q: Ignorant devotees, who worship Allah in ways He did not prescribe while thinking it brings them closer to Him, are nearest to which group at the end of al-Fatiha?
quiz|1|final|6|c0: Those who are astray: they act without knowledge
quiz|1|final|6|c1: Those who have earned anger: they know and do not act
quiz|1|final|6|c2: Those who have been blessed: they know and act
quiz|1|final|6|why: They have sincerity without following and act out of ignorance, and the ignorant are those who are astray.
quiz|1|final|7|q: Why does the one praying ask for guidance in every rak'ah, when they are already praying on the straight path?
quiz|1|final|7|c0: Because clarification of the path has not yet reached them
quiz|1|final|7|c1: Because they ask for more success and for steadfastness until arriving
quiz|1|final|7|c2: Because general guidance can be cut off
quiz|1|final|7|why: Specific guidance is clarification, then success granted, then steadfastness; the traveller needs at every moment more success and steadfastness in the face of trials.
quiz|1|final|8|q: The Qadariyyah said Allah treated His allies and His enemies alike in help. In what is this sameness true?
quiz|1|final|8|c2: In general lordship and general mercy
quiz|1|final|8|why: Allah supports both groups with His general lordship and His general mercy, whereas specific success is for His allies.
quiz|1|final|9|q: What links the plural form in ﴿اُ۪هْدِنَا اَ۬لصِّرَٰطَ اَ۬لْمُسْتَقِيمَ﴾ (Guide us to the straight path) and the mention of ﴿صِرَٰطَ اَ۬لذِينَ أَنْعَمْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ (the path of those You have blessed)?
quiz|1|final|9|c0: Comfort in companionship, removing the traveller's loneliness of being alone
quiz|1|final|9|c1: That the people of truth are the most numerous
quiz|1|final|9|c2: That guidance is collective, not individual
quiz|1|final|9|why: People are by nature lonely when alone, so the servant asks guidance for themselves and for others, and recalls the company of the prophets, the truthful, the martyrs and the righteous.
quiz|1|final|10|q: Who is the best of the four kinds regarding “You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help”?
quiz|1|final|10|c0: Someone who seeks Allah's help for their worldly shares and desires
quiz|1|final|10|c1: Someone who makes worshipping Allah the goal of all they want, and asks Him to help them in it
quiz|1|final|10|c2: Someone who worships Allah and thinks they do so by their own might and strength
quiz|1|final|10|why: The people of “You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help” have joined worship and seeking help, which is why one of the best supplications is: “O Allah, help me to remember You, to thank You and to worship You well.”
